districts.notes: District-center city Hilla included as nahiya. Al-Kifl is now its own district.
Newer district. Jabla is also known as Al-Mashroua' (المشروع).
The census-based list (قائمة نواحي العراق) additionally lists Al-Khamisiya (الخميسية) and Al-Husayn (الحصين) as nawahi of this district; unverified.
Newer district (was a nahiya of Hilla District in the census list).

governorates.notes: 7 districts per Arabic Wikipedia (محافظة بابل). Kutha and Al-Kifl are newer districts (post-2019 map). Sources: ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/محافظة_بابل administrative table, ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/قائمة_نواحي_العراق (census-based list).

districts.notes: Awn stayed with Karbala District; per a 2009 council decision it was initially assigned to Al-Husseiniya District.
Al-Rahhaliya listed on the governorate article; the census list shows only the district center.
Subdistrict list could not be verified; only agricultural مقاطعات (land plots) are documented. District confirmed by ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/قضاء_الحر.
Al-Taf (الطف / الجرية) confirmed under this district per ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/ناحية_الطف.

governorates.notes: 5 districts per Arabic Wikipedia (محافظة كربلاء). Al-Husseiniya upgraded from nahiya to district in 2009; Al-Hurr is also now a district. The census-based list (قائمة نواحي العراق) still shows only 3 districts and predates these upgrades.

districts.notes: Al-Radhawiya and Baniqia are newer nawahi not present in the census-based list; confirmed in official 2023 exam-result publications.

governorates.notes: 4 districts per Arabic Wikipedia (محافظة النجف). Governorate infobox claims 12 nawahi; 8 nawahi verified (6 in census list + Al-Radhawiya and Baniqia, post-census nawahi confirmed by Iraqi Ministry of Education 2023 exam results).
